honesty: All 48 values below are MODEL-PRODUCED and UNREVIEWED. No gate in this repo can see translation quality -- lint-translations checks key PRESENCE only, and nothing in CI detects English-side or translation-side drift. A green gate over this file means 48 non-empty strings exist at the right key, and nothing more. The executor applies `locales.<code>.value` verbatim and must NOT author, adjust or 'improve' any value.

method.corpus_gap: 260927-q9t-corpus.json carries only the first, third and fourth of those. A fifth in-namespace parallel exists in all 49 gamelib catalogs and was surveyed live at planning time: `settings.eosOverlayUpdateConfirmBody` ('Update EOS Overlay to the latest version?'). It supplies the update verb the fork itself already chose, in the same namespace as the new key, and it CHANGED FOUR VALUES away from what the corpus alone would have produced -- `fa` (gamelib spells the verb به‌روزرسانی with a ZWNJ, translation.json spells it spaced), `ja` (gamelib uses 更新, translation.json uses アップデート), `ml` (gamelib spells അപ്ഡേറ്റ് with NO zero-width non-joiner), and `nl` (gamelib uses 'bijwerken', translation.json uses the loanword 'updaten'). It also turned `br`, `hr`, `sk`, `sl`, `ta`, `th` and `fi` from authored guesses into in-namespace derivations.
method.noun_phrase: The subject noun-phrase is taken from that locale's own `gamelib:setting.eosOverlay.unavailable` -- namespace-internal terminology consistency, because the new key lives in the same `gamelib.json` subtree as its only sibling. This is the rule even where `translation.json` renders 'EOS Overlay' differently, which it does in roughly 28 of the 46 locales that have both files (e.g. `ar` gamelib 'طبقة EOS Overlay' vs translation 'واجهة إي.أو.إس'; `fr` "L'overlay EOS" vs "L'interface Epic Online Services (EOS)"; `zh_Hant` 'EOS Overlay' vs 'EOS 內嵌介面'). Accepted, recorded cost: in those locales the new status line names the overlay differently from the three sibling status lines the same widget renders. That cross-namespace divergence pre-dates this task, is visible in the shipped UI today, and is not this task's to fix.
method.predicate: The update verb comes from `gamelib:settings.eosOverlayUpdateConfirmBody` where it is decisive, otherwise from `translation:setting.eosOverlay.updating`, normalised out of any first-person or bare-gerund form that cannot carry a full sentence (e.g. `cs` 'Aktualizuji...' is 1st person -- rendered reflexive as 'se aktualizuje'; `vi` 'Đang Cập Nhật...' is title-cased -- lowercased to match its own installing sibling).
method.agreement: NP-GENDER AGREEMENT RULE. Where the predicate carries gender/number inflection (a participle or predicative adjective), it must agree with the noun-phrase ACTUALLY SHIPPED -- the gamelib one -- and NOT with the noun-phrase of the translation.json string the pattern was lifted from. Those two are different nouns in roughly 28 locales, so an inflection copied across unchanged is a live agreement bug. The authority for the shipped NP's gender is that locale's own gamelib catalog, and `setting.eosOverlay.unavailableDetail` is the strongest witness because it inflects three participles against this exact noun ('cannot be installed, updated or removed'). This rule caught one defect on review -- see `agreement_audit`.
method.pattern: The sentence pattern is taken from that locale's own `translation:setting.eosOverlay.installing` -- the nearest sibling with the same progressive aspect, rendered by the same widget.
method.ellipsis: The glyph comes from that locale's own `translation:setting.eosOverlay.installing`. Measured across the 46 locales that have it: 41 use '...', and `bg`/`ca`/`de`/`hu`/`ja` use '…' (`de` with a preceding space). Where that string is absent, empty, or an English passthrough it carries NO signal for the locale -- `br`/`sl` have no translation.json at all, `ka`/`th` have the key empty, and `hr`/`ml`/`sk` left it byte-identical to English. Those seven fall back to the dominant convention of the file the new string actually lives in, that locale's own gamelib.json. Measured across all 49 gamelib catalogs: '…' dominates every single one (14-19 occurrences vs 0-2 of '...'), and in `sl` alone the dominant multi-word form carries a space before it (10 of 17).
method.english_exception: `en` keeps three dots ('...') to match `translation:setting.eosOverlay.installing` in English -- the same sibling-status-line rule applied to English, as the task brief directs. Note the measured tension this creates and does not resolve: the `en` gamelib catalog is itself 15 '…' to 1 '...', so the new English value is the minority convention in its own file while being the matching convention in its own widget. The widget won. The English value is NOT in this artifact: it is minted by `pnpm i18n` from the `tGamelib()` default at the call site.

agreement_audit.reason: Post-review sweep for one specific class: a locale whose NP was taken from gamelib but whose predicate inflection was carried over from a translation.json sibling built on a DIFFERENT, gendered native noun. Every locale with gendered predicate agreement was re-checked against its own gamelib catalog.

findings.gl: UNCHANGED. The pattern source's NP is feminine ('a superposición'), but the value uses a GERUND ('Estase actualizando'), which carries no agreement, so nothing could be carried over.
findings.no-inflection group: UNCHANGED, no exposure: cs/sk/sl/hr/bs/sr/ru/uk/ro use a 3sg reflexive or plain finite verb; pl uses the prepositional 'jest w trakcie aktualizacji'; be's grammatical subject is the neuter noun 'абнаўленне' with the NP in the genitive; it's subject is the masculine noun "l'aggiornamento" under the invariable 'è in corso'; ca uses a gerund; he ('בעדכון') and ar ('قيد تحديث' + iḍāfa) are nominal. es and pt_BR were already masculine against masculine NPs, with no NP swap in the source.
findings.outside the candidate set: Swept too, no exposure: da/nb_NO/nl/de/sv participles are invariable here, fi/et are impersonal passives, el/bg are gender-neutral verb forms, and ga's 'á + nuashonrú' is unaffected because n- never lenites. Every remaining locale is genderless.
